study type: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
exposure: Thermal manual methods (including cold packs and intermittent hot and cold packs)
cohort: The study included data from 1055 women in labour across 10 randomized controlled trials investigating manual methods for pain management.
finding: Massage, warm packs, and thermal manual methods may reduce pain and length of labour, and improve women's sense of control and emotional experience during labour, although the evidence quality is low to very low.
mod_finding: Low to very low-quality evidence suggests no clear benefit of manual methods, such as massage or thermal manual methods, on the rates of assisted vaginal birth or caesarean section.
